findings.title: REVIEW_RECEIPT.json carries contradictory pre-correction provenance claims
findings.detail: REVIEW_RECEIPT.json correctionStatus.note (L193) claims 'Review candidate directory retains PRE-CORRECTION frozen copy for review continuity', and qaPostCorrectionResult (L204) = 'PENDING — QA rerun after corrections'. Frozen-byte evidence contradicts both: all 12 corrected files match REVIEW_RECEIPT_CORRECTIONS.json 'files' map (the corrected/SYNCED variant), and that receipt's qaPostCorrectionResult (L97) asserts the post-correction QA PASSed (226 assertions, 0 failures). REVIEW_RECEIPT_CORRECTIONS.json L92 does explicitly supersede the stale fields ('Corrected candidate is SYNCED into review-candidate (not a frozen pre-correction copy)… Authoritative hashes are the 'files' map in this receipt'), and the 5ac7d9aa commit message calls the prior claims 'aspirational handoff claims' — but REVIEW_RECEIPT.json was never reconciled in-file, so a consumer reading it alone receives false provenance and a wrong hash table (see F3).
findings.reference: REVIEW_RECEIPT.json:193 (correctionStatus.note), REVIEW_RECEIPT.json:204 (qaPostCorrectionResult), REVIEW_RECEIPT_CORRECTIONS.json:92 (correctionStatus.note supersession + authoritative 'files' map), REVIEW_RECEIPT_CORRECTIONS.json:97 (qaPostCorrectionResult PASS), git 5ac7d9aa message
